solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Monument featured in newspaper article?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tall pillar raised as a memorial, like Nelson's
second meaning: a regular piece written for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A monument gets a write-up in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that both halves are definitions of one word rather than a story about a monument in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a memorial pillar and a regular piece of journalism in a newspaper.

clue.text: Horse has groom removing marks

indicators.note: removing says the following letter is taken out of the grooming word

parts.note: to groom hair is to comb it
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A horse owner's stablehand grooms away the marks on its coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes M (marks) out of COMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob is a sturdy, short-legged breed type of riding horse.

clue.text: Fine material right for Queen to wear — it's glossy

indicators.note: to wear means the material and right put on, i.e. around, the Queen's letters

parts.note: lace is a fine open fabric

explanation.surface: A fine fabric suitable for royalty is described as shiny.
explanation.walkthrough: QU as a short form of Queen is less familiar than ER or R; 'for' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a varnish that dries to a hard shiny finish.

clue.text: Wicked deeds of some nursemaid being naughty

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is unruly, so the letters of the two words misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: A nanny's misbehaviour is listed as a catalogue of bad acts.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirteen letters of SOME and NURSEMAID rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Misdemeanours are minor wrongdoings or offences, a mild sense of wicked acts.

clue.text: Showing sign of injury, having lost heart, being frightened

indicators.note: heart is the central letter, so the middle letter of the seven-letter word is dropped

parts.note: skin marked by a healed wound is scarred

explanation.surface: Someone wounded and dispirited is now afraid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' drops the middle R of SCARRED; 'being' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared is a plain synonym for afraid or alarmed.

clue.text: Thought to show respect for others?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: careful reflection on a matter
second meaning: thoughtfulness about other people's feelings

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'Thought' and 'respect for others' are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deliberation before deciding and kindly regard for the needs of other people.

clue.text: Type associated with Catholic Church?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ordinary upright style of printing type, as opposed to italic
second meaning: the ... Catholic Church is centred on Rome

explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like 'sort', but it is printer's type.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman names upright printed lettering and also describes the Church headed by the Pope in Rome.

clue.text: Ado with eldest abused, made very unhappy

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fuss in which the oldest child is mistreated leaves someone miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ADO and ELDEST together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolated means overwhelmed with grief or misery, deeply wretched.

clue.text: County briefly in the money

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the short form of Buckinghamshire, an English county north-west of London
second meaning: slang for dollars, money

explanation.surface: A wealthy English shire is said to be rolling in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckinghamshire is a home county west of London, usually shortened to Bucks; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the standard short name for an English shire and also slang for dollars or cash.

clue.text: Mum's after awfully nice places of entertainment

indicators.note: after puts the mother's letters following the jumbled word
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of nice are jumbled

parts.note: Mum is MA, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A mother follows on to some very pleasant venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' reads as an intensifier for 'nice', but it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinemas are venues where people go to watch films for amusement.

clue.text: Bird that's top, not bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry the last letter is the bottom one, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head or of a hill

explanation.surface: A bird that rules the roost, never the lowest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not bottom' removes the last letter, N, from CROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow is a large black member of the corvid family.

clue.text: Wild animal captured by Magnus

indicators.note: captured by means the answer is held inside the name that follows

explanation.surface: A beast is caught by a man called Magnus.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal sits inside the name: maGNUs.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is an African antelope that lives wild on the plains.

clue.text: Soldier in terrible danger, one with little sign of hesitation

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of danger are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
er is the little sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A soldier, facing grave peril, barely hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'with' are just links joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is an infantryman, originally one who threw grenades, now a Guards regiment member.

clue.text: Eastern movement has a learner aroused?

parts.note: motion means movement
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: An Oriental exercise routine excites a student.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a martial art like tai chi; 'aroused' is the definition, its question mark flagging a slightly loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone emotional has their feelings stirred up, which is one way of being moved or excited.

clue.text: The Queen entertaining a composer, a moneymaker

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them, so the composer goes inside the Queen

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: Royalty plays host to a musician who brings in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: ER = Elizabeth Regina; Thomas Arne, an 18th-century English composer, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is something, like a job or product, that brings in income.

clue.text: Some Parisian with big belly, a tyrant

parts.note: des is French for some, as a Parisian would say it
a pot is a paunch or pot belly

explanation.surface: A paunchy Frenchman is an oppressor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some Parisian' points at French: des is the French word for 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute, often cruel, power.

clue.text: Joker gets better around end of performances

indicators.note: around puts the gambler's letters on either side of the picked letter

parts.note: a better here is one who bets, a punter

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of performances

explanation.surface: A comedian improves over the run of shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'improves' but is someone who bets: PUNTER goes around S, the last letter of performances.
explanation.definitionFit: A punster is someone given to wordplay jokes, a teller of puns.

clue.text: Sort of school greeting being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the greeting is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: A school is known for its spoken welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: HI said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A high school is a secondary school, so the word describes a kind of school.

clue.text: A right fellow to have in a country

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A decent chap would be welcome in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but here the pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America.

clue.text: Obtain at university a set of clothing

parts.note: to obtain is to get
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Buy a whole outfit while studying.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, a student is 'up' at university when in residence.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is an outfit, especially an unusual or elaborate one.

clue.text: Refusal by daughter to give sign of agreement?

parts.note: no is a refusal
D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A girl's refusal is oddly taken as consent.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a 'no' becomes a sign of 'yes'; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head shows assent or approval.

clue.text: One part of the Bible with biblical hero, verily

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
NT is the New Testament
Ruth is the heroine of the Old Testament book named after her

explanation.surface: Scripture and its heroes, delivered in solemn old language.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth is a woman, so 'hero' is used loosely for heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Verily is an archaic word for truly or indeed, the same as the phrase.

clue.text: Bury's football team a long way from Bury!

definitions.text: football team a long way from Bury
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ... Milan, an Italian football club far from Bury, a town near Manchester

explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester with its own football club, so 'Bury's football team' looks like Bury FC; the exclamation mark points to a team far away.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to place in a grave, and the short name for Milan's Internazionale club.

clue.text: Painful conflict to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so the word is turned back

parts.note: war is conflict

explanation.surface: A sore struggle up in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw describes skin that is sore and tender, stinging to touch.

clue.text: Break in which old man gets meal

indicators.note: in which says the father goes inside the break

parts.note: a rest is a break
old man is slang for father, PA

explanation.surface: During a pause, Dad has something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or old-fashioned word for a meal.

clue.text: A knight portrayed as a saint

parts.note: N is knight in chess notation
to portray is to draw, past tense drew

explanation.surface: A knight is depicted as a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the chess abbreviation for knight, since K is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew is one of the apostles and the patron saint of Scotland.
